question.prompt: The corpus does not provide the web entry URL for the TodoMVC app, which every runnable web test needs as its first step.

options.label: Use variable
options.detail: Author the tests against a placeholder start URL variable such as {{start_url}} until the runtime environment supplies it.

options.label: Provide URL
options.detail: Supply the actual web start URL to replace the placeholder in the tests.

content.risk_rationale: Without a start URL, the tests for this web use-case cannot run at all even though the feature behavior is otherwise specified.

question.prompt: The corpus does not state how test data with High and Low priorities is made available, and this use-case has no priority-editing flow to create those values during the test.

options.label: Assume seeded tasks
options.detail: Author scenarios and tests assuming the environment provides at least one visible task with High priority and one visible task with Low priority.

options.label: Provide setup source
options.detail: Supply a source or setup reference that explains how High- and Low-priority tasks are created or seeded.

content.risk_rationale: Allowed-value coverage is incomplete without a way to surface non-default priorities, but the default-Medium behavior can still be designed.

question.prompt: The PRD says the task-card UI, controls, and layout stay as they are today, but the corpus does not define a measurable baseline for today's layout beyond the existing checkbox and delete control.

options.label: Use control compatibility
options.detail: Treat this promise as preserving the existing completion checkbox and delete "x" control only, and leave broader layout sameness out of the executable oracle.

options.label: Provide baseline artifact
options.detail: Supply a screenshot, DOM contract, or spec excerpt that defines the current task-card layout to compare against.

content.risk_rationale: The source expresses a regression-sensitive promise, but without a baseline artifact any broader layout oracle would be guesswork.

question.prompt: The PRD describes the priority indicator as a small badge but does not give a measurable size rule or reference style.

options.label: Use badge-style check
options.detail: Treat "small" as a semantic badge-style indicator and do not assert pixel dimensions or typography thresholds.

options.label: Provide size rule
options.detail: Supply a measurable size threshold or reference style for what counts as a small badge.

content.risk_rationale: Visual size affects fidelity, but the core product behavior is the presence and value of the badge rather than a specific pixel dimension.

content.text: Each task card displays a visible priority badge.

expected_answer.operand: task card has a visible priority badge

content.text: Each displayed priority badge value is High, Medium, or Low.

expected_answer.operand: priority badge text is one of High, Medium, or Low

content.text: A task with no explicit priority set shows Medium on its badge.
Each task card still exposes its completion checkbox.

expected_answer.operand: task card has a completion checkbox

content.text: Each task card still exposes its delete "x" control.

expected_answer.operand: task card has a delete "x" control

judgements.rationale: [risk_factors] Applied user-reach to all acceptance criteria because every user who views task cards sees the badge state. Applied change-frequency because this enhancement directly modifies task-card chrome and is therefore regression-prone. Did not apply money, auth, or data-loss because the source only describes display of priority labels on a TodoMVC task card.
